Jacob Abel competed in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES in 2026 for the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500, driving the No. 51 Chevrolet for Abel Motorsports and his father, Bill Abel. He made his debut in the series in 2025 with Dale Coyne Racing, posting a career-best 11th at Iowa Speedway.

A product of the INDYCAR development ladder, he finished second in INDY NXT by Firestone in 2024, earning three wins and three poles with his family-run team. Away from the track, he enjoys cycling and lacrosse – a sport he played in high school – along with skiing, tennis and golf. He attended Butler University in Indianapolis.

Despite giving up racing to play hockey at age 11, he stayed involved in the sport through sim racing. In 2020, he attended an SCCA racing school as a high school graduation gift. By the end of racing school – a one-time opportunity from his parents -- he was running track record times and had reignited his passion for racing. He won SCCA National Titles in Formula Ford (2023) and Formula Continental (2022-23) and raced in Britain’s highly competitive BRSCC Formula Ford National Championship in 2023, winning his heat race and pole at the prestigious Formula Ford Festival. Allaer balances racing with being a full-time college student. He’s a senior at Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, working toward a degree in mechanical engineering.

Bryce Aron returns to Chip Ganassi Racing for his third season in INDY NXT by Firestone. He earned one podium, three top-five and eight top-10 finishes in his 2024 debut and added one top-five and six top-10 finishes in 14 starts in 2025. The 21-year-old Illinois native previously raced in Euroformula Open, finishing fourth with three wins and two podiums, and in GB3. He also won the 2024 Formula Regional Oceania Championship. Off track, Aron enjoys running, cheering on the Chicago Blackhawks and following college football.

Jack Beeton makes his U.S. debut with HMD Motorsports in INDY NXT by Firestone in 2026. The 18-year-old Gold Coast, Australia native joins the series after a rookie season with PREMA Racing in the Formula Regional European Championship by Alpine, earning multiple podiums and a race win. Beeton also finished second in the Italian F4 Championship and won the Formula 4 South East Asia Championship.

American-Ecuadorian driver JM Correa enters his second full-time season in INDY NXT by Firestone in 2026, joining Cusick Morgan Motorsports for their inaugural venture in the series. The Miami native, a Rotax Grand Finals champion, advanced through Formula 4, Formula 3 and Formula 2 before finishing fifth at the 12 Hours of Sebring with United Autosport. In 2025, he made nine INDY NXT starts, earning a podium in only his third race on the Streets of Detroit and adding three top-10 finishes.

Salvador De Alba joins Andretti Global for his second season in INDY NXT by Firestone after making his debut with Andretti Cape INDY NXT in 2024. The Mexican driver began his professional racing career in 2016 in the Super Copa Telcel series, earning Rookie of the Year honors that season. He then continued his success while racing in the Tractocamiones Freightliner and NASCAR Mexico Series, winning the NASCAR Mexico championship in 2021 and 2023. De Alba also recently became a five-time Super Copa GTM Champion, holding the 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 titles. He began his open-wheel racing career in 2022 competing in the USF Pro 2000 Presented by Continental Tires series and placed third in the development series’ driver championship in 2023.

Alessandro de Tullio joins AJ Foyt Racing for its two-car return to the INDYCAR development series in partnership with HMD Motorsports. He completed his first full season in USF Pro 2000, finishing fourth in the standings. In 2024, De Tullio made six USF Pro 2000 starts and won SKUSA Winter Series titles in both X30 Pro Senior and KA Senior classes. His background also includes a full season in USF Juniors.

Mexico City native Ricardo Escotto rejoins Juncos Hollinger Racing for the 2026 INDY NXT by Firestone season. The 21-year-old previously competed with the team during a five-race stint in mid-2024 before contesting most of the 2025 campaign with Andretti Cape. Escotto returns to JHR as the organization prepares for its return to INDYCAR’s top development series. He began his racing career in 2017 in senior karting on the SKUSA tour and made his open-wheel debut in the NACAM Formula 4 Championship in 2018, earning two top-10 finishes in three starts. His résumé also includes competition in Spanish Formula 4 and UAE Formula 4 in 2022, where he finished inside the top five in the Rookies’ Championship standings.

Carson Etter enters the 2026 INDY NXT by Firestone season with Chip Ganassi Racing. The California native moves up after racing in USF Pro 2000 in 2025. An Arizona State University student, Etter began in off-road Pro Lite competition before moving to open-wheel racing in the F4 Formula Pro USA Western Championship, where he earned five wins and 12 podiums. He completed his 2024 USF2000 rookie season with four top-10 finishes.

Brazilian Enzo Fittipaldi continues the storied Fittipaldi family legacy in North American motorsports, joining INDY NXT by Firestone with HMD Motorsports in 2026. The grandson of two-time Formula One World Champion and two-time Indianapolis 500 winner Emerson Fittipaldi and brother of former F1 and INDYCAR driver Pietro Fittipaldi, he carries one of racing’s most iconic surnames. Fittipaldi, a former Italian F4 champion and FRECA runner-up with Ferrari Driver Academy, advanced through Formula 3 and Formula 2, earning two wins and 13 podiums in F2 as part of the Red Bull Junior Team, where he remains a Red Bull athlete. In 2025, he gained further experience racing in the European Le Mans Series with CLX Motorsport and participating in INDYCAR and Formula E test sessions.

2025 USF Pro 2000 champion Max Garcia joins ABEL Motorsports for his first INDY NXT by Firestone season. The Florida native began with Pabst Racing’s USF2000 team in 2023, earning two podiums in a partial rookie season. In 2024, he claimed five wins and 10 podiums to capture the series title and became the youngest ladder system scholarship winner at 15. Garcia surpassed that in 2025, scoring nine wins, nine poles and 13 podiums in 18 races while completing every lap of the season.

Bart Harrison makes his U.S. debut with HMD Motorsports in INDY NXT by Firestone in 2026. The 18-year-old British driver joins the series while also competing as a rookie in the Eurocup-3 championship. Harrison has competed in GB3, British F4, Italian F4 and E4 and won two races in CEZ F4 at Red Bull Ring.

Gold Coast, Australia native Lochie Hughes returns to Andretti Global for his second INDY NXT by Firestone season in 2026 after an impressive rookie campaign. In 2025, Hughes collected two wins, two poles, eight podiums, 54 lead laps and 12 top-10 finishes, including a victory from his first career pole at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and a charge from fifth to first in his oval debut at World Wide Technology Raceway. His consistent performances earned him third in the championship. Hughes previously won the 2024 USF Pro 2000 Championship.

Nikita Johnson joins Cape Motorsports for his first full-time INDY NXT by Firestone season after three appearances with HMD Motorsports in 2025. The Florida native raced in four open-wheel series across three continents in 2025, including Formula Regional Oceania, British GB3 and FIA Formula 3. He became the youngest-ever British GB3 winner in 2024 with a victory at Zandvoort, followed by another at Brands Hatch. Johnson finished second in the 2024 USF Pro 2000 championship with eight wins and was runner-up in USF2000 in 2023. He also became the youngest USF Pro 2000 race winner at Circuit of the Americas in 2023 at age 15.

Colin Kaminsky joins ABEL Motorsports for his first full-time INDY NXT by Firestone season after select appearances in 2023. The Illinois native made his INDY NXT debut that year, competing in eight of 14 rounds with three top-10 finishes. In 2024, he raced in the Porsche Carrera Cup North America Championship. Kaminsky did not compete professionally in 2025, instead launching Kaminsky Park, a corporate venue and go-kart facility in Monticello, Indiana.

Niels Koolen returns in 2026 with Chip Ganassi Racing for his third INDY NXT by Firestone season. The son of rally-raid driver and Dutch businessman Kees Koolen, he began karting at 14 and gained experience in Formula Regional European and Middle East championships, European Le Mans, FIA Formula 2 and select Spanish and Italian F4 races. Koolen finished the 2025 INDY NXT season with a top-five and seven top-10 results. He is managed by A-14 Management, the driver development academy founded by two-time Formula 1 World Champion Fernando Alonso.

Alexander Koreiba transitions to open-wheel competition in 2026 following a successful stint in sports car racing, highlighted by capturing the 2024 HSR Prototype Challenge presented by IMSA championship and competing in the IMSA Prototype Challenge. A Missouri native, he began karting at 14 before advancing through the Lucas Oil School of Racing and into professional prototype competition. Along the way, he has balanced driving with mentorship, coaching young drivers and working with racing enthusiasts across the country.

Polish driver Tymek Kucharczyk will make his INDY NXT by Firestone debut with HMD Motorsports in 2026, racing in America for the first time. The 19-year-old becomes the first Polish driver to compete in the INDYCAR development series after a dominant 2025 campaign, winning the Euroformula Open Championship with BVM Racing. Kucharczyk began karting at age 5 and quickly emerged as a standout talent. His formula racing career includes a third-place finish in the 2022 F4 Spanish Championship with one win and 12 podiums, followed by two seasons in the GB3 Championship, where he earned four wins, three poles and third in the championship standings.

Jordan Missig returns for his second full-time INDY NXT by Firestone season in 2026 with ABEL Motorsports. He won the 2024 Radical Cup North American Series Championship with nine wins and 16 podiums with Graham Rahal Performance and the Radical Indianapolis team and finished third in the Radical World Finals in Abu Dhabi. Missig advanced to INDY NXT after racing in USF Pro 2000, Lamborghini Super Trofeo, Formula Regional Americas and karting. In 2025, he scored six top-10 finishes and placed ninth in the championship. The Illinois native enjoys cheering on the Chicago Blackhawks and playing pickleball. He lives at Autobahn Country Club, where he works as director of the driving academy, and serves as an ambassador for Racing For Mental Health, a non-profit founded by his parents.

Nicholas Monteiro joins INDY NXT by Firestone for his first full-time season as AJ Foyt Racing returns to the INDYCAR development series. Monteiro, a Brazilian-American, made his series debut at Portland in 2025 and brings experience from USF Pro 2000 from 2023–25, as well as previous stints in the Brazilian and Italian F4 Championships.

Seb Murray begins his second INDY NXT by Firestone season with Andretti Global. The Scottish driver completed his rookie 2025 campaign with two top-10 finishes and one top-five, overcoming a mid-season setback after an on-track incident at Mid-Ohio sidelined him for the Iowa round. Murray returned for the Laguna Seca doubleheader, qualifying eighth for both races and earning his first top-five finish in Race 2. Prior to INDY NXT, he competed in the 2024 F4 UAE season, scoring a top-five finish, and then raced in the GB3 Championship, making 24 starts and finishing as high as seventh.

Italian Matteo Nannini returns to INDY NXT by Firestone for the 2026 season. He won the 2019 Formula 4 UAE Championship at age 16, claiming seven victories and the title by 48 points. Nannini then competed in Formula 3 in 2020 and 2021, capturing a win in Hungary in 2021, before moving to the ARCA Menards Series in 2022. He made his INDY NXT debut in 2023 with Juncos Hollinger Racing, earning a win at Indianapolis Motor Speedway before parting ways with the team midseason. In 2025, Nannini launched ENVE Motorsports, which competed in the final race of the USF2000 Championship season, finishing 15th.

Josh Pierson enters his third full-time INDY NXT by Firestone season in 2026 and his first with Andretti Global. The Portland, Oregon native debuted in 2023 and had his most successful campaign in 2025, scoring two podiums and 11 top-10 finishes to place sixth in the championship. Pierson also competed in F1600 in 2020, U.S. F2000 in 2020–21 and the 2025 Formula Regional Oceania Championship, earning multiple podiums and consistently finishing in the top 10. He has experience in sports car racing, including IMSA and the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2022–23, capturing multiple podiums and competing twice in the 24 Hours of Le Mans, with a best finish of 10th.

James Roe returns for his fifth INDY NXT by Firestone season in 2026 and his first with Chip Ganassi Racing. He emigrated from Ireland to the U.S. at 19 and began racing at 15, with experience in FIA F4 UAE, F2000, FIA Formula Regional Americas and USF Pro 2000. Roe aims to advance to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES and the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. Off track, he lives in Indianapolis, enjoys Notre Dame football and works with Ireland Funds, a nonprofit supporting Irish social programs, including sports initiatives.

Myles Rowe returns for his third INDY NXT by Firestone season and second with ABEL Motorsports. The 2023 USF Pro 2000 champion races with Force Indy, a pilot program of Penske Entertainment’s Race for Equality and Change. Rowe began in karting and added titles, including the Lucas Oil School Formula Car Race Winter Series. Following a suggestion from two-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion Will Power, he joined Force Indy, achieving success in USF2000 (2021–22) and USF Pro 2000 (2023). In 2021, he became the first Black driver to win an INDYCAR-sanctioned race, and in 2025 he earned his first INDY NXT win at Iowa Speedway, becoming the first Black driver to win in the series. He finished 2025 with two wins, 10 top-five finishes and fourth in the championship. Rowe graduated from Pace University Manhattan in 2022 with a degree in film and screen studies.

Seventeen-year-old Australian Nicolas Stati makes his INDY NXT by Firestone debut in 2026 with Cusick Morgan Motorsports. He has competed internationally in Formula Regional Oceania, Formula Regional Americas, GB3, F4 U.S., F4 U.A.E. and F4 Australian Championships. In 2024, Stati finished as vice champion in both the F4 U.S. and F4 Australian Championships, falling just 4 1/2 points short of the U.S. title.

Yuven Sundaramoorthy returns to INDY NXT by Firestone in 2026 with Cusick Morgan Motorsports at World Wide Technology Raceway. A full-time driver in USF PRO 2000 in 2023, Sundaramoorthy made the jump to INDY NXT by Firestone in 2024, finishing 8th in the championship. Aside from his racing career, Yuven completed his bachelor of science degree in computer science at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2023 as a full-time student. He broke ground by becoming the first Indian American driver to win an INDYCAR-sanctioned event at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, in 2021 and 2022 in the USF2000 Championship.

Aside from racing, Sundaramoorthy channels his passion for sports by playing volleyball, basketball and soccer. He also keeps up with his home state Green Bay Packers and Milwaukee Bucks. In addition, he likes golf, snowboarding and robotics. Sundaramoorthy also spent six years of his childhood living in China and is fluent in Mandarin.

Max Taylor enters his first full INDY NXT by Firestone season in 2026 with Andretti Global. In 2025, he raced full-time in USF Pro 2000, earning one win, four podiums, nine top-five and 13 top-10 finishes in 18 races, while also making six INDY NXT starts with one top-five and four top-10 results. The Greenwich, Connecticut native began his open-wheel career in 2023 in USF Juniors, finishing sixth with one win, three podiums and six top fives, while also competing part-time in USF2000 and the Formula 4 U.S. Championship. In 2024, he captured the USF Juniors Championship, placed third in USF2000 and made three GB3 starts, with a best finish of 11th.
